Definition: from G3638 and G2250; an eight-day old person or act:--the eighth day.
BiblicalUsage: Oktaemeros means of the eighth day, circumcised on the eighth day. Paul uses it once, in Philippians 3:5, listing his own marks: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's eighth day proves that no pedigree saves, and the man who had every mark counted them all as loss.
